# Distill long emails: Telegram & Notion

**Pattern:** AI Summarize & Route · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers invoices work end to end across Telegram and Notion.

It moves through 14 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. On Telegram Event
2. Read Recent from Notion
3. Newest First
4. Trim to Digest Size
5. Summarize Content (AI)
6. Groq Chat Model
7. Post Digest to Telegram
8. Archive Digest in Notion
9. Stamp Processing Time
10. Tag Pipeline Metadata
11. Align Field Names
12. Summarize Run Stats
13. Append Audit Row (Notion)
14. Send Summary to Telegram

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Telegram — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing invoices work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

On Telegram Event → Read Recent from Notion → Newest First → Trim to Digest Size → Summarize Content (AI) → Groq Chat Model → Post Digest to Telegram → Archive Digest in Notion → Stamp Processing Time → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Align Field Names → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Notion) → Send Summary to Telegram → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Telegram

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Telegram and Notion aligned by hand for invoices
- Pushing invoices events into Telegram and Notion the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Invoices work where "Read Recent from Notion" is still a manual step before Telegram
- Invoices work that only reaches Telegram when a webhook arrives, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Telegram and Notion in step for invoices, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Telegram or Notion call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 16 nodes in this invoices build
- The invoices AI step is isolated from Telegram, so models swap without touching the other 16 nodes
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 16 nodes for invoices before wiring Telegram
- 16 nodes, each with a doc card explaining what it does for invoices

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Groq API key; Notion integration token; Telegram bot token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Summarization uses a Chain, not an Agent, because the step is fixed — there's no decision about which tool to call, just 'summarize this text.' Posting to multiple channels runs as parallel branches, not sequential sends, so a slow API on one channel never delays the message that was already ready on another.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Add a third notification channel and watch the Merge node's input count update.
2. Change 'Trim to Digest Size' from 15 to 5 and see how it narrows the summary's scope.
3. Swap the Summarization Chain for a Q&A Chain to answer questions instead of just recapping.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Telegram bot token**
Same bot token as the Telegram node (@BotFather → /newbot).
_Gotcha:_ A bot supports only one webhook at a time — a second workflow listening on the same bot steals the updates.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Groq API key**
console.groq.com → API Keys.
_Gotcha:_ Very fast and cheap, but with tight per-minute rate limits.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your invoices process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Telegram: the bot token is a bearer credential — rotate it if it ever appears in an execution log.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole invoices payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.
